governing_equations.equation: UA_cond = (k / t) * A, q = UA_cond * (T_box - T_skin)
governing_equations.basis: Fourier steady conduction through a plane wall.

governing_equations.equation: h = h0 * sqrt(p(alt)/p(0)), q = h A (T_skin - T_amb)
governing_equations.basis: Natural convection; h0 an assumed small-enclosure value (category D), scaled by the square root of the pressure ratio.

governing_equations.equation: q = eps * sigma * A * (T_skin^4 - T_rad^4), T_rad = T_amb - offset
governing_equations.basis: Stefan-Boltzmann. The offset collapses Earth/horizon/space view factors into one parameter (category D).

governing_equations.equation: UA_cond (T_box - T_skin) = h A (T_skin - T_amb) + eps sigma A (T_skin^4 - T_rad^4)
governing_equations.basis: Conduction and surface loss are IN SERIES. Solved each step by bisection.
Lumped-capacitance. C_th sums pack, insulation and housing mass x cp.

governing_equations.equation: P_pv = I_direct(alt, elevation) * A_panel * eta * view
governing_equations.basis: Beer-Lambert attenuation of extraterrestrial irradiance. Solar HEATING of the box structure is NOT modelled — see limitations.
Assumed fraction (category D), applied to DELIVERED power only.

governing_equations.equation: usable = charge - nominal*(1 - f(T));  P_max = C_rate * Ah * V
governing_equations.basis: Capacity curve is an assumption (category D).

benchmarks.title: Lumped-capacitance decay vs closed-form solution
benchmarks.category_label: Analytical verification -- compared against a closed-form solution
benchmarks.method: Forward Euler advanced to a fixed final time at four timesteps and compared with the closed-form solution. Error must fall as dt falls.

conditions.order_note: Forward Euler is first-order. The observed order is measured against the exact closed form, so unlike the mission-level study in app/verify.py this reference is not itself an approximation.

benchmarks.reference: T(t) = T_inf + (T0 - T_inf) exp(-t/tau), with UA_eff derived by hand as a series combination of conduction and convection.
limitations: Exact only because radiation is disabled; the radiative term is not exercised by this benchmark.
UA_eff is treated as constant, so this does NOT verify the altitude-varying convection or the temperature-dependent terms.
This verifies the integrator and the conduction/convection network. It says nothing about whether k = 0.030 W/m/K is the real value for the box (category D).

benchmarks.title: Stefan-Boltzmann radiation against the exact expression
benchmarks.category_label: Analytical verification -- compared against a closed-form solution
benchmarks.method: Direct comparison of the implementation with the closed-form expression.
limitations: Verifies the arithmetic, not the view factors. The real payload sees Earth and horizon as well as space; that is collapsed into a single assumed radiant temperature offset (category D).
Assumes the skin is isothermal and grey.

benchmarks.title: Equilibrium solver vs an independent root find
benchmarks.category_label: Analytical verification -- compared against a closed-form solution
benchmarks.method: Engine bisection compared with an independent bisection written in this file, plus the residual at the returned root.
limitations: Both solvers call the same heat_loss_w routine, so this verifies the root-finding, not the loss model itself.
Equilibrium assumes the ambient is constant, which a real ascent is not. The bench protocol in bench/ measures this quantity, which is why it is the right comparison for a future physical test.

Several of these configurations equilibrate ABOVE the 60 C maximum operating temperature. That is not a solver error: a well-insulated box with a standing 5 W heater genuinely overheats. It is why the engine has a TEMP_ABOVE_OPERATING failure mode.

benchmarks.title: Limiting cases and heat-flow direction
benchmarks.category_label: Analytical verification -- compared against a closed-form solution
benchmarks.method: Direct evaluation of limiting cases with asserted expected behaviour.
benchmarks.reference: Second law of thermodynamics and the monotonicity of a series conductance network.

items.check: passive equilibrium matches closed-form skin balance
items.expected: T settles at -66.190 C, i.e. BELOW ambient, not at it
items.note: Radiative cooling to a sink colder than the air drives the box below ambient. Settling above ambient with zero heat input would violate the second law.

limitations: These are invariants, not quantitative accuracy checks: they catch a sign error or a broken monotonicity, not a wrong magnitude.
The 'balanced' tolerance of +/-0.5 W exists because the radiant sink is colder than the air, so a box at air temperature still loses a little.

benchmarks.title: Engine ISA vs published US Standard Atmosphere 1976
benchmarks.category_label: Independent reference comparison -- external published source
benchmarks.method: Direct value-by-value comparison with the published reference table.

conditions.engine_model: linear lapse to 11 km, isothermal above

benchmarks.reference: US Standard Atmosphere 1976 / ICAO ISA reference table (15 degC and 1013.25 hPa at sea level, 6.5 K/km to 11 km, 216.65 K isothermal above).
limitations: The engine is isothermal above 11 km, so it is exact through 20 km and DIVERGES above it: the real atmosphere warms from ~20 km and reaches 228.65 K at 32 km. The engine is not used as a data source above the forecast ceiling except as a declared fallback, and this table shows where that fallback is weakest.
ISA is a reference atmosphere, not a forecast for any particular night.

task2_energy.category_label: Numerical / software verification -- convergence, invariants, regression
task2_energy.sign_convention: Positive = energy LEAVING the battery, or heat ENTERING the payload node. Electrical: storage_drop + pv_into_cells + unmet_energy - payload_delivered - heater_delivered = residual. Thermal: heat_in - heat_lost + heat_gained - stored_change = residual.
task2_energy.note_thermal: The thermal residual is identically zero for forward Euler: the scheme's own accumulation reproduces it term for term. It is a BOOKKEEPING CONSISTENCY identity, NOT an accuracy measure. Euler truncation error is quantified in Task 1 (analytical) and Task 4 (convergence).

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: Heater energy was booked at the COMMANDED power, not the power the pack actually delivered. When the pack hit its C-rate limit the reported heater consumption exceeded the energy the battery supplied.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: heater_energy_wh accumulated heater_w (the thermostat request) while the pack was only able to supply p_max.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Delivered power is now split explicitly: payload first, heater from the remainder; all bookkeeping uses delivered values.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: Payload self-heating was computed from the commanded load even when the pack could not supply it, creating thermal energy from nothing.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: payload_heat_w was computed once, outside the loop, from the design value.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: payload_heat_w is now derived each step from delivered_payload_w.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: Reported heat loss clamped negative flow to zero (max(0, q)), silently discarding every heat-GAIN interval and reconstructing the total from 1-minute samples instead of the integration itself.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: heat flow is now accumulated in the loop from the same q that drove the step, split into heat_lost and heat_gained.

task3_battery.source_status: The capacity-vs-temperature curve is an ASSUMPTION. It is shaped like commonly published Li-ion behaviour but is NOT taken from a datasheet held for the specific cells used, and NO cell was tested at any temperature. Do not describe it as datasheet-verified.
unmeasured_parameters: Capacity at each temperature below 20 C
Internal resistance vs temperature (affects the C-rate ceiling in the cold)

task3_battery.required_before_any_flight_claim: A datasheet for the exact cell part number, and ideally a discharge test at low temperature. Until then the battery model is category D.

task6_uncertainty.disclaimer: These are SCENARIO PASS RATES over assumed input ranges. They are not probabilities of real-world survival. The ranges were chosen to bound engineering plausibility, not measured.

unresolved: Box thermal conductance UA is UNVALIDATED. It derives from an assumed conductivity and an assumed geometry; no bench measurement exists.
The battery capacity-vs-temperature curve is an ASSUMPTION. No specific cell datasheet is attached and no cell was tested.
The radiant temperature offset is a single parameter standing in for full view-factor geometry. It is the largest uncertainty in the loss path.

Solar heating of the enclosure is not modelled; daytime results are biased cold. Night survival results are unaffected. The model computes solar ELECTRICAL generation only, so a sunlit payload is never warmed.
The engine's ISA is isothermal above 11 km and therefore diverges from the published standard atmosphere above about 20 km (see benchmark B1).
Thermal residual in the energy balance is an identity for forward Euler and is not an accuracy measure; real truncation error is quantified in Tasks 1 and 4.
Overheating failure mode is modelled but has never been observed in flight.
Uncertainty ranges are exploratory and are not probability distributions, so no survival probability is reported anywhere in this project.
Category E (physical experiment) is empty. No bench test was conducted.
